identity.description: Latent-regime model over sequences: hidden states follow a Markov chain, each state emits observations from a parametric distribution (Gaussian or categorical). EM (Baum-Welch) fits states + transitions jointly; the validated Predictive Studio use is member activity-cadence regime as a downstream feature via the latent-state adapter.

consumes.note: per-entity ordered observation frames; hmmlearn convention is concatenated X + a lengths vector — the adapter owns that packing
single-entity regime detection — a lone series is the one-sequence degenerate case; the adapter wraps it

emits.note: posterior state probabilities (gamma) per observation; argmax gives the pointwise state. THE validated feature emission: activity-cadence state via the latent-state -> features:tabular adapter
Viterbi most-likely joint path — NOT the same as pointwise argmax of the posterior
fitted transmat_ over the LATENT alphabet; interpretable only after canonical state ordering (label switching)
per-sequence log-likelihood — low-likelihood paths are the anomaly-flavored secondary use

n_components.note: state count — selected by BIC/held-out log-likelihood, the family's model-selection lens; NOT by training likelihood, which rises monotonically in K

covariance_type.note: Gaussian variant only; full costs O(d^2) params per state

n_iter.note: EM iteration cap; check monitor_.converged, not just completion

n_restarts.note: wrapper-level multi-restart, best-of by log-likelihood — the hedge against EM local optima that makes deterministicFit false

min_covar.note: covariance floor preventing state collapse onto single points

invariances.why: diag-covariance emissions (the default) and k-means-style EM initialization both depend on the relative scale of observation dimensions; unstandardized channels dominate the fit
Gaussian emission likelihood is not preserved under nonlinear monotone maps — log-transforming an observation channel changes which regimes are separable
Baum-Welch needs complete observation vectors at every step; hmmlearn has no missing-observation update
CategoricalHMM requires symbols pre-coded to 0..K-1 integers; the Gaussian variant is numeric-only — encoding is still a pipeline concern
assumes first-order Markov dynamics on the HIDDEN chain plus a parametric (Gaussian/categorical) emission law per state
each state's emission parameters are estimated from the observations it occupies; total corpus length under ~50-100 observations per state leaves states unsupported and EM degenerate
out-of-range observations decode to whichever state's emission tail is nearest — mechanically defined but carrying no principled beyond-range structure

featureStats.why: mixture structure in the observation marginal is the fingerprint of distinct emission regimes; a unimodal marginal warns that K>1 states may be an EM artifact
temporal persistence is what separates an HMM from a plain mixture — near-zero autocorrelation means a GMM explains the data without the transition machinery
corpus length divided by candidate K is the effective sample per state; below a floor, emission params are unidentifiable — a gate to smaller K

modelMetrics.why: training likelihood rises monotonically with K; BIC's penalty on the K^2 transition + emission params is the honest state-count selector
mean self-transition probability — regimes that flip every step are label noise, not latent structure; diagonal dominance is what makes the state a usable cadence feature
spread of converged log-likelihoods across random restarts measures likelihood multimodality — high dispersion says the chosen fit is one local optimum among many

edgeCases.condition: EM fails to converge within n_iter

edgeCases.behavior: state indices permute — 'state 2' means different things run to run
edgeCases.note: canonicalize state order (by emission mean, then persistence) before persisting latent-state features

edgeCases.condition: degenerate state (near-zero occupancy or collapsing covariance)
sequences concatenated without a lengths vector
edgeCases.behavior: silent spurious transitions across entity boundaries
paths cannot visit enough states to inform transitions

driver.constructor: GaussianHMM(n_components, covariance_type, n_iter, min_covar).fit(X, lengths) / CategoricalHMM(n_components, n_iter).fit(X, lengths); best-of n_restarts by score
driver.wrapperNeeds: sequence adapter: per-entity ordered frames -> concatenated X + lengths; multi-restart loop with seed control; canonical state reordering for stable labels; latent-state -> features:tabular adapter for the validated activity-cadence-as-feature use
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded fit per model; run restarts as parallel processes

canBeSeeds.via: latent-state -> features:tabular adapter (per-entity current-regime + occupancy shares)

placementClaims.why: no native missing-observation update — gaps must be filled (time-aware) or sequences segmented before Baum-Welch
log-transforming skewed activity counts makes per-state Gaussian emissions plausible, sharpening regime separation
standardizing observation channels keeps diag-covariance emissions and EM initialization from being dominated by the largest-scale channel
CategoricalHMM needs symbols integer-coded 0..K-1; the Gaussian variant is numeric-only, so categoricals must be encoded or dropped
